open_errors.issue: After the Fair, Meera 'slipped away' along the river ice until the crowd's noise was a hum, and Rohan 'found her' there. They are still rope-bound until the thaw and cannot separate beyond eight spans, so she cannot leave him behind in the crowd and he cannot come looking for her.
open_errors.fix: Have the rope draw Rohan along with her, so they are never apart.

patches.find: Meera slipped away. She walked until the noise was a hum, along the river ice to the lee of a half-fallen wall, and sat down on it.
patches.replace: Meera slipped away, and the rope drew Rohan out of his sister's hands after her. She walked until the noise was a hum, along the river ice to the lee of a half-fallen wall, and sat down on it.

patches.find: He found her there within a few breaths. He could not have gone farther, with eight spans of rope. He stood a little way off, and she saw he had taken off his gloves.
patches.replace: He reached her within a few breaths. He had never been more than eight spans of rope behind. He stood a little way off, and she saw he had taken off his gloves.

open_errors.issue: In ch 24 the buyer says Varun crossed the Saddle bound at the Shilak Cairn to a salt-road man. In ch 25 Varun says he has heard of a jogini binding but never seen one, and asks whether it holds.
open_errors.fix: Let Varun speak as a man who has just been bound himself.

patches.find: and he whistled. "A jogini binding! On the Shilak! I'd heard of it, never seen one."
patches.replace: and he whistled. "A jogini binding! I wore one myself to come over, but I never thought to see you in one."

patches.find: He walked the length of the cord with his eyes. "And it holds? She can't leave you?"
patches.replace: He walked the length of the cord with his eyes. "And it holds you the way it held me? She can't leave you?"

open_errors.issue: In ch 25 Varun arrives in 'a new coat, the grey of the regent's house, with a brass button at the throat.' The Fair evidence in ch 28 and ch 30 depends on the single new brass button among the pewter ones on his old coat, and ch 30 shows exactly that coat.
open_errors.fix: Keep Varun in his old coat with the brass button among the pewter ones.

patches.find: He had a new coat, the grey of the regent's house, with a brass button at the throat that caught the light.
patches.replace: He had his old coat brushed clean, the pewter buttons dull in a row, and the one brass button among them caught the light.

open_errors.issue: The eighteen courses began about a week earlier and have run out. One of them was Sunni's, and she is dead. The patients who are mid-course now are the twenty-three who started the buyer's redbark the night before.
open_errors.fix: Change the mid-course figure to the twenty-three on the buyer's redbark.

patches.find: Seven marked houses on the lane. Forty-one sick, eighteen of them mid-course, and every one of them lying behind a wall of planks.
patches.replace: Seven marked houses on the lane. Forty-one sick, twenty-three of them one night into the buyer's redbark, and every one of them lying behind a wall of planks.

open_errors.issue: Varun tells Meera she 'roped up the gully ahead of me.' In ch 3 the party crossed the gully unroped, one at a time, thirty paces apart. No one was roped until the cairn.

patches.find: "Jassi's second," said Varun. "You roped up the gully ahead of me. What are you doing here?"
patches.replace: "Jassi's second," said Varun. "You walked the gully ahead of me. What are you doing here?"

open_errors.issue: Kiran says Dilan and he were bound with knots on their wrists. He then says Dilan cut the rope 'above his waist', which is a leftover of an earlier waist-to-waist roping. Rohan's piece is only a forearm's length of rope from Dilan's end.
open_errors.fix: Place the cut near Dilan's wrist.

patches.find: Then he had his knife. He cut his own rope above his waist, and it went slack, and I stopped.
patches.replace: Then he had his knife. He cut his own rope close to his wrist, and it went slack, and I stopped.

open_errors.issue: In ch 27 Rohan's bound promise is 'I won't ask you anything else about that rope.' Ch 28 describes it as a promise of no more questions at all. Rohan asks Meera ordinary questions in ch 29, 30 and 31 ('May I?', 'What are you counting?', 'What?'), and under that reading each would break a bound promise.
open_errors.fix: Restate the promise with its actual scope.

patches.find: He had promised her no more questions, and he meant to keep the promise down to its smallest corner.
patches.replace: He had promised her no more questions about that rope, and he meant to give the promise a wide berth.

open_errors.issue: Ch 31 says the bond ends 'after the first drip at the cairn'. The rule, stated plainly in ch 32, is that the bond ends when meltwater first runs at the cairn: 'A drip was not meltwater running.'

patches.find: After the first drip at the cairn it would be only a rope.
patches.replace: Once meltwater ran at the cairn it would be only a rope.

open_errors.issue: Rohan has been captain for more than ten years. Varun held his horse when he was newly captain, and Dilan died at 23. Dilan's oath therefore came under Rohan's captaincy, and Rohan gives the punishment himself, so 'the old captain' does not fit. The post's senior officer is elsewhere called the post commander.
open_errors.fix: Change 'the old captain' to the post commander.

patches.find: He laughed in the middle of the oath at the post, in front of the old captain.
patches.replace: He laughed in the middle of the oath at the post, in front of the post commander.

open_errors.issue: Meera recalls that 'Rohan wrote that the law was for the next one.' In ch 31 Rohan says this aloud after writing the clause. He does not write it.

patches.find: When Rohan wrote that the law was for the next one, Kiran had nodded and said nothing until the ink dried.
patches.replace: When Rohan said the law was for the next one, Kiran had nodded and said nothing until the ink dried.
